analysis: Examined the test-only change in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Tools/FlintNativeProtocolTests.swift. Head lines 209-226 add a test asserting that FlintNativeProtocolConstraint opts into chained decoding (allowsChainedDecode), returns nil maskCacheKey for remainingTokens=0 and out-of-range states (cachedStateCount), and that identical keys map to identical allowed-token masks across modes auto/none/required. Head line 267 asserts that maskCacheKey is nil after state-pool exhaustion, which preserves the fail-closed behavior: exhaustion cannot become a cacheable mask or a normal EOS. No production source is included in this batch. The implementations of maskCacheKey, allowsChainedDecode, and the mask cache consumer live outside the supplied evidence. The new tests exercise only a test vocabulary and do not touch the threat model's assets. In particular, they do not affect A-001 encryption, TB-002 or TB-011 authorization, attestation, or the T-041 prefix cache. The relevant concern is integrity and availability of constrained decoding within TB-007. Integration should verify that the production mask cache key does not alias two distinct masks across requests or states, for example by including the constraint instance or vocabulary identity, mode, allowed tools, and remainingTokens. If the cache is shared across tenants, verify it cannot leak tool schemas or allow an unconstrained token. Also verify that chained decode preserves the per-step nextState validation that the native constraint enforces for tool-call execution boundaries. Because these tests add no new attack surface and the implementation is not visible, no regression was identified.
